intro.title: Component Library Theming
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a themed component library in Angular by creating a reusable button component that can change its appearance using custom properties. You will learn how to use Angular's @Input decorator to pass theme data from a parent component to a child component, allowing for dynamic styling. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and CSS custom properties for theming. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible, themeable UI components that can adapt to different design systems.
intro.usecase: Component theming is essential for creating consistent, branded interfaces across enterprise applications. In real-world Angular projects, you'll implement theming systems for admin dashboards where different user roles need distinct color schemes, or e-commerce platforms requiring holiday-themed UI variations. Developers use these patterns to build design systems that maintain visual consistency across components like data tables, modals, and navigation menus while allowing quick rebranding. This approach enables teams to efficiently support multiple client brands or dark/light mode preferences without rewriting component styles.
